clue.text: Doctor of literature is 24- no point retiring

parts.note: the clue at 24 down is the rebel leader of the Peasants' Revolt, whose first name was Wat

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the words no and point are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A literary scholar is told he is like some rebel, with his pen retreating pointlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' turns NO + S (point) into SON, placed after WAT. The doctor is Sherlock Holmes's companion, a doctor in literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Holmes's narrator and friend in Conan Doyle's stories is a medical man, a doctor found in fiction.

clue.text: Othello, we hear, after a love affair

indicators.note: after places the sounded piece behind the letter A
we hear signals that a word is said aloud, and the spelling entered differs

parts.note: Shakespeare's Othello is the Moor of Venice

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's jealous general is pursued by a romance, rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: MOOR said aloud gives the sound of MOUR, which follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for love is used in English for a romantic, often secret, liaison.

clue.text: It may raise the level of our spirits

definitions.text: It may raise the level of our spirits

parts.words: It may raise the level of our spirits
parts.note: spirits here are whisky or brandy in a glass, and a mixer topped up makes the liquid in the glass rise

explanation.surface: Something that cheers us up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' reads as mood, but it means alcoholic drinks; adding a fizzy mixer raises the level in the glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbonated water is a mixer poured into whisky, filling the glass higher.

clue.text: Idea of climbing-it fills in time

indicators.note: fills in says one piece is put inside another so as to occupy it

parts.note: midday, noon, is a time of day

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going upwards, so the word it is read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A thought about mounting something that takes up a slot in the schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing' turns IT into TI, and 'fills in' puts TI inside NOON.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is a concept or thought in the mind.

clue.text: Sea breezes bear Tom home

definitions.meaning: light airs that ruffle the water's surface in small patches
a tomcat's feet carry him back home

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is the phrase cat's paws: Tom is a male cat, and his paws carry him home.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors name a light breeze rippling calm water after the mark of a feline foot; feet carry an animal along.

clue.text: Epistle-reader, gives us this reference

parts.note: a lesson reader in church announces exactly which book, section and line of the Bible the epistle comes from

explanation.surface: A church lesson reader cites where the passage is found.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase also means a precise citation of authority for any statement.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bible passage is located by its numbered section and line, and the phrase now means exact sourcing.

clue.text: Brown must replace outside right giving displays of petulance

parts.note: tan is a brown colour

indicators.note: outside says the rearranged letters go round the letter for right
replace means the letters of the word must are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A man named Brown has to stand in for the outside-right player and shows bad temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replace' rearranges MUST as TUMS, and 'outside' wraps it round R to give TRUMS, after TAN. Outside right is a winger's position in old football line-ups.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantrums are childish fits of temper, outbursts of petulance.

clue.text: Demonstration, in quiet part of building

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
the roof is the top part of a building

explanation.surface: A protest held in a hushed section of some building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demonstration' suggests a protest march, but here it means showing something to be true.
explanation.definitionFit: A proof is a demonstration that establishes a fact.

clue.text: Figures men are fakers? That's about right

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to wangle is to fake or fiddle, so wanglers are fakers

explanation.surface: Someone claims that men who deal in figures are frauds, and agrees it is about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts R inside WANGLERS. At Cambridge, a wrangler is a student gaining first-class honours in mathematics, hence a man of figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge's top mathematics graduates are called by this name, so they are numbers experts.

clue.text: Transport sought by poultry breeder perhaps

definitions.meaning: a breeder of hens wants a fine line of stock, a sound bloodline

explanation.walkthrough: Split differently, the letters read GOOD STRAIN, which a chicken breeder would want.
explanation.definitionFit: A freight railway service carries cargo; a quality breeding line is what a stock raiser seeks.

clue.text: Ground appears ill-omened to batsmen ?

definitions.meaning: a cricket ground in south London
the shape of a nought on the scoreboard, a duck, is a batsman's dread

explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground; a nought, the score a batsman fears, is egg-shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: Kennington's famous sports venue bears this name; a zero is an egg-shaped figure that batsmen dread.

clue.text: A large number want our organization to be extended

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

indicators.note: organization means the letters of want and our are arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: Many people want our society enlarged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organization' rearranges WANT OUR as RAWNOUT, after D.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prolonged or stretched in time is said to be lengthy in this way.

clue.text: It might be taken from pursuers

definitions.text: It might be taken from pursuers

parts.words: It might be taken from pursuers
parts.note: fugitives take shelter to escape those chasing them

explanation.surface: Something seized from those giving chase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken from' looks like snatched away, but the idiom is to take shelter from.
explanation.definitionFit: A refuge is a shelter one takes when fleeing.

clue.text: The bird for speed ?

definitions.meaning: a wading shore bird of the sandpiper family
a unit of speed at sea, one nautical mile an hour

explanation.definitionFit: A wader of the sandpiper family shares its name with the nautical speed unit.

clue.text: Book of the month — on eastern race in general

parts.note: Nov is the abbreviation for November

indicators.note: in puts the race inside the general's name

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general
TT, the Tourist Trophy, is a motorcycle race

explanation.surface: A book club's monthly choice concerns oriental racial matters in broad terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book of the month' looks like the definition, but only 'Book' defines; 'in' puts TT inside LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelette is a short novel, a slight book.

clue.text: Said to make money abroad in backing animals

indicators.note: in says the money goes inside the reversed animals
backing means the word for animals is turned backwards

parts.note: deer are animals
the mark was German currency

explanation.surface: Words about earning foreign cash by betting on horses or dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' turns DEER into REED, and 'in' puts MARK inside it. 'Backing animals' suggests betting at the races.
explanation.definitionFit: To remark is to say or observe, so the past tense means said.

clue.text: Bill may be dead ?

definitions.meaning: an account of what is owed
navigators' dead ... estimates position from speed and course

explanation.walkthrough: Dead reckoning is navigation without fixes; 'dead' is not about a person named Bill dying.
explanation.definitionFit: An account presented for payment, and the calculation of position at sea known as dead reckoning.

clue.text: Sporting official rows to island

parts.note: rows are lines
the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A referee's assistant paddles towards an isle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' looks like a verb of rowing a boat, but it is a noun meaning lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A linesman assists the referee in football or tennis, watching the boundaries.

clue.text: Dislike Ivan Roe's arrangement

indicators.note: arrangement means the letters of the two names are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Ivan dislikes how Roe has organized things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrangement' rearranges IVAN ROES.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong distaste or dislike.

clue.text: The plight of a boxer ?

parts.note: plight means predicament, and a boxer here is one who boxes things, i.e. packs them in a container

explanation.surface: A fighter's sorry state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' suggests a fighter, but it is someone who puts things in boxes; the word for that container also means a situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A predicament or state of affairs, and also a container a packer would fill.

clue.text: Swamp quarter on lake

parts.note: S, south, is one quarter of the compass
lough is the Irish word for a lake

explanation.surface: A marshy district by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts S above LOUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a muddy bog or marsh.

clue.text: Thanks predecessor ?

parts.note: a polite request comes before the thanks in the usual pairing of courtesies

explanation.surface: Gratitude to the person who held the job before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Predecessor' suggests a former office-holder, but it means the word said before 'thank you'.
explanation.definitionFit: A courteous word of request is said before the expression of gratitude.

clue.text: Extent of a matutinal morsel ?

parts.note: matutinal means of the morning, and a.m. stands for morning
a bit is a morsel

explanation.surface: How large is a breakfast nibble?
explanation.walkthrough: Matutinal means relating to the morning, abbreviated AM.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambit is the scope or range of something.

clue.text: Virginia takes, money, opening a Firbank work

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
L stands for pound, from the Latin libra
a mouth is an opening

explanation.surface: Virginia takes the cash and launches a novel by Ronald Firbank.
explanation.walkthrough: Ronald Firbank was an English novelist; Valmouth (1919) is one of his novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Valmouth is the title of a 1919 novel by Ronald Firbank, a literary work of his.

clue.text: Rebel leader: comes in rarely — the retiring type

indicators.note: retiring type says the lettering runs backwards, retiring meaning going back
comes in says the answer is found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A rebel chief rarely attends: he is the shy sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes in' finds RELYT inside 'rarely the', and 'retiring type' reverses it. Wat Tyler led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381.
explanation.definitionFit: He led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381, an uprising against the poll tax.

clue.text: Only a direction to return the counterfoil

indicators.note: to return means the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: but means only, as in 'but a child'
S, south, is a direction

explanation.surface: Just one instruction to send back the ticket slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To return' reverses BUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A stub is the part of a ticket or cheque kept as a record.

clue.text: Animals found in pumas' lairs, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of the two words could be ordered differently

explanation.surface: Creatures discovered in the dens of big cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges PUMAS LAIRS.
explanation.definitionFit: Kangaroos and koalas are pouched mammals, a class of animals.

clue.text: Perhaps a fine bit of writing?

definitions.meaning: a fine is one kind of punishment a court passes
a grammatical unit of written words

explanation.walkthrough: 'Writ' within writing hints at law, which fits the first sense: a punishment handed down.
explanation.definitionFit: A court's penalty, such as a fine, and a grammatical unit of prose.

clue.text: Goddess embraces soldier of Mohammedan era

indicators.note: embraces says the goddess's name goes round the soldier

parts.note: Hera was queen of the Greek gods
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A goddess hugs a soldier in a story of Islamic times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embraces' puts GI inside HERA. The Hegira is Muhammad's flight to Medina in 622, from which the Islamic calendar counts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Islamic calendar dates years from the Prophet's flight to Medina, so the term names that era.
